ADA.citation: Cardano is a separate L1; IOHK/Cardano Foundation does not operate an XRPL issuer. Any XRPL ADA is impostor. Reference: https://cardano.org.

BNB.citation: BNB is native to BNB Chain (formerly Binance Smart Chain). Binance does not issue XRPL representations of BNB. Any XRPL BNB is community-issued impostor. Reference: https://www.bnbchain.org.

BONK.citation: https://xrpldashboard.com/methodology — meme-name policy: XRPL BONK tokens reuse the Bonk name; no canonical issuer exists.
BONK.note: meme name — XRPL BONK tokens reuse the name, not a backing claim

BTC.citation: Bitcoin is native to the Bitcoin blockchain; there is no Bitcoin Foundation / Bitcoin Core organization that issues XRPL representations. The legitimate XRPL 'BTC' rails are custodial IOUs from long-standing gateways — GateHub (whitelisted below) and Bitstamp (whitelisted below). Any BTC ticker on a non-gateway issuer is impostor. Reference: https://bitcoin.org (Bitcoin's canonical protocol page — no XRPL issuance).

DAI.citation: DAI is Sky/MakerDAO's stablecoin on Ethereum (with wrapped presences on other L2s via Sky Protocol). Sky does not operate an XRPL issuer. Any XRPL DAI is impostor. Reference: https://sky.money (chain support does not include XRPL).

DOGE.citation: https://xrpldashboard.com/methodology — meme-name policy: XRPL DOGE tokens reuse the Dogecoin name; there is no cross-chain canonical Dogecoin issuer on XRPL (Dogecoin is a native L1). Absence from canonical_issuers is intentional per this policy.
DOGE.meme_name_note: 2026-09-12 (Charlie ruling): collision rule narrowed to identity-bearing assets only (stablecoins, wrapped/bridged majors, brand/exchange names). Memecoin name reuse is expected practice on XRPL and deceives no one about backing. Meme-name matches get category=memecoin and no warning; kept internally as meme-name-reuse curator-queue tag.
DOGE.note: meme name — XRPL DOGE tokens reuse the name, not a backing claim

ETH.citation: Ethereum is native to its own L1 blockchain; there is no Ethereum Foundation XRPL issuer. Legitimate XRPL 'ETH' rails are custodial gateway IOUs (GateHub — whitelisted below) or wrapped-bridge representations (Midas/Axelar — whitelisted in bridges). Any bare ETH on a non-gateway non-bridge issuer is impostor. Reference: https://ethereum.foundation (Ethereum Foundation site — no XRPL issuance).

LINK.citation: LINK is Chainlink's Ethereum-native token with CCIP-bridged presences on multiple chains — XRPL is not on Chainlink's supported chains list. Any XRPL LINK is impostor. Reference: https://chain.link/

LTC.citation: Litecoin is native to its own blockchain; the Litecoin Foundation does not issue XRPL representations. Legitimate XRPL LTC rails are custodial gateway IOUs (GateHub — whitelisted below). Bare LTC from non-gateway issuers is impostor. Reference: https://litecoin.org.

MATIC.citation: MATIC / POL is native to Polygon PoS; Polygon Labs does not issue an XRPL representation. Any XRPL MATIC is impostor. Reference: https://polygon.technology.

PEPE.citation: https://xrpldashboard.com/methodology — meme-name policy: XRPL PEPE tokens reuse the Pepe name; no canonical issuer exists.
PEPE.note: meme name — XRPL PEPE tokens reuse the name, not a backing claim

RLUSD.citation: https://xrpldashboard.com/rlusd — curator note (2026-09-22): this XRPL issuer (rMxCK…) is the on-XRPL canonical for the ticker string "RLUSD" but is NOT Ripple's official RLUSD stablecoin (which is issued primarily on Ethereum). Ripple has not confirmed an official XRPL RLUSD issuer to us. The site's /rlusd page explains both entities.

SHIB.citation: https://xrpldashboard.com/methodology — meme-name policy: XRPL SHIB tokens reuse the Shiba Inu name; no canonical issuer exists on XRPL.
SHIB.note: meme name — XRPL SHIB tokens reuse the name, not a backing claim

SOL.citation: Solana is native to its own L1 blockchain; the Solana Foundation does not issue an XRPL representation. Legitimate XRPL SOL rails are bridge-issued via Midas/Axelar (whitelisted in bridges section). Bare SOL from non-bridge issuers is impostor. Reference: https://solana.com/ (no XRPL bridge listed).

TETHER.citation: Same as USDT entry — Tether does not issue on XRPL. Any XRPL TETHER is a community-issued IOU. Reference: https://tether.to/en/supported-protocols.

TRX.citation: TRX is native to the Tron blockchain; the Tron Foundation does not issue an XRPL representation. Any XRPL TRX is impostor. Reference: https://tron.network.

USDC.citation_note: Circle's own multichain USDC page lists this XRPL mainnet address for native USDC (fetched 2026-09-12). Prior canonical_issuers=[] treated the empty list as positive knowledge and rendered 'not Circle USDC' on the real Circle issuer 2026-09-06 to 2026-09-12. Added tonight per Charlie's ruling.

USDT.citation_note: Tether's own supported-chains page (accessed 2026-09-12): USDT is issued on Ethereum, Tron, Solana, TON, Avalanche, BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Near, Cosmos, Kaia, and others — XRPL is not on the list. Any USDT on XRPL is a community-issued IOU, not Tether Inc. There IS a self-claimed USDT via usdxrp.net at rHjUEuGTbiSc2KowsvATgfFQwP8rWGyMvK; the conflict rule handles that case with 'unverified — conflicting records'.

USDX.citation: USDX is used by multiple unrelated stablecoin projects (Kava, Ethena's USDe variant, etc.); no single 'canonical' issuer exists cross-chain, and none of them operate on XRPL. Any XRPL USDX is a community mint reusing the ticker.

WBTC.citation: WBTC is BitGo's Ethereum-native wrapped-BTC token. The legitimate XRPL wrapped-BTC representation is Midas/Axelar's WBTC (whitelisted in bridges section) — a bridge product, not the original WBTC. Bare WBTC from non-bridge issuers is impostor. Reference: https://wbtc.network (no XRPL issuance).

XLM.citation: Stellar is a separate L1 blockchain; the Stellar Development Foundation does not operate an XRPL bridge or issue XLM on XRPL. Legitimate XRPL XLM rails are custodial gateway IOUs (RippleFox — whitelisted below). Bare XLM from non-gateway issuers is impostor. Reference: https://stellar.org (no XRPL bridge listed).

_bridges_doc: Bridge/wrapped-asset issuers that legitimately mint XRPL-side representations of off-chain tokens. When a token's issuer is in a bridge's issuers list AND its decoded ticker is in that bridge's tickers list, resolve_display() treats it as canonical (no collision label) with category = wrapped_bridge. This overrides the collision path — a WBTC issued by an Axelar/Midas bridge is the bridged form, not a collision claim against mainstream WBTC. Added 2026-09-08 after row #4 (SOL from rfmS3zqr...) surfaced in the curator queue as a false-positive collision.
_doc: Curated map of well-known off-chain tickers → their canonical XRPL issuers (if any). Read by token_naming.resolve_display(). When a decoded currency name matches one of these keys but the issuer is NOT in canonical_issuers, /token, /whales, /check etc. render the collision-qualified form (e.g. 'USDT (usdxrp.net — not Tether)'). canonical_issuers=[] means NO canonical XRPL issuer exists — every match is a collision. Add cautiously; a new entry retroactively re-qualifies every existing display.
_gateways_doc: Custodial fiat/BTC/ETH gateway issuers on XRPL — same collision-override semantics as bridges section (bridge-issued tickers → canonical, not collision), but distinct category (stablecoin_gateway) for editorial clarity. Populated conservatively as of 2026-09-08 — only issuers with strong evidence (matching domain + long-standing public address) are whitelisted here. Two-way toml proof walker has not yet run against these issuers as of add-date (domain_two_way_proof='unchecked'), so citations lean on domain match + historical public knowledge. Any addition here should specify: issuer address(es), tickers they issue, citation URL to the issuer's own published address page (or their xrp-ledger.toml).
_source_of_truth: Ripple's RLUSD launch announcement (2024); public issuer registries at xrpscan.com and xrplf.org/registry (spot-checked 2026-09-06). Update this file, not code, when a legitimate issuer changes hands.

bridges.citation: https://xrpldashboard.com/methodology — umbrella row explaining the category; not a specific ticker.

midas_xrpl.citation: curator-verified 2026-09-08 (Charlie ruling). Existing token_category_history entries for this issuer at wrapped_bridge tier since 2026-09-06 seed cover 8 of these tickers (SOIL, USDC.axl, USDf, WBTC, WETH, mBTC, mTBILL, mXRP); SOL + SHX added by this bridges section to keep the collision-check code aligned with the curator seed.
midas_xrpl.name: Midas / Axelar bridge — XRPL wrapped assets
midas_xrpl.note: Bridge-issued XRPL representations of off-chain assets. Ticker match here is the bridged form, not a collision — do NOT set ticker_collision=TRUE for these (issuer, ticker) pairs.

gateways._disputed_vanity_addresses: The addresses rBASE5KtDVqaWCTpQatezWfc4cZV7eDuyB (domain www.coinbase.com), rCoinzYTFiFMJ5qyPPXSieGYbLACw9tnM (domain https://www.coinbase.com/), rKRAKzWfCB1SA1Pz24HGUVJ8reMEeCsMEG (domain https://www.kraken.com) all use vanity-address prefixes but Kraken/Coinbase don't publicly operate XRPL gateway issuance. They look like impostor vanity registrations claiming brand affiliation. NOT whitelisted — will remain in curator_review_queue with the ticker_collision flag set.

bitstamp.citation: AccountRoot Domain field = 'bitstamp.net' (issuer_facts snapshot 2026-09-08); long-standing public address (see https://xrpscan.com/account/rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B). Bitstamp deprecated new XRPL-side issuance around 2018 but the outstanding tokens remain tradeable; USD IOU shows 10,962 trades in trailing 30d, BTC shows 5,487 — clearly still-in-use custodial-gateway rails. Two-way toml proof pending — add when the walker runs against this issuer.
bitstamp.name: Bitstamp — historic XRPL fiat/crypto gateway
bitstamp.note: Historic gateway. USD + EUR are fiat-backed custodial rails; BTC + ETH are the gateway's issuance of those tickers (not native, not collisions in the impostor sense).

gateways.citation: https://xrpldashboard.com/methodology — umbrella row explaining the category; not a specific ticker.

gatehub.citation: GateHub's own published XRPL address page at https://gatehub.net/legal/xrpl-addresses (accessed 2026-09-11 by Charlie via screenshot). 16 hot + 16 cold wallets across 17 currencies; USD and EUR share the same hot/cold pair (rhotcWYdfn6qxhVMbPKGDF3XCKqwXar5J4 + rhub8VRN55s94qWKDv6jmDy1pUykJzF3wq). Tier stays self-described per Charlie's ruling — the canonical whitelist stops the collision flag but does NOT promote these to verified. Two-way toml proof pending (domain_two_way_proof='unchecked' at add-time). Retires the 2026-09-08 `_todo_gatehub` placeholder.
gatehub.name: GateHub — XRPL fiat/crypto gateway
gatehub.note: Long-standing XRPL gateway. Every (issuer, ticker) pair from these 32 addresses × 17 tickers is treated as canonical — ticker_collision must NOT be set. Fiat rails (USD/EUR/GBP) + crypto rails (BTC/ETH/etc.) + newer tickers (XAH/EVR from Xahau ecosystem). GALA / FLR / SGB are gaming/L1 project tokens on GateHub.

ripplefox.citation: AccountRoot Domain field = 'ripplefox.com' (issuer_facts snapshot 2026-09-06); site content at https://ripplefox.com/ self-describes as an XRPL and Stellar gateway operating since 2014 ("始于2014年"). Long-standing Chinese-language gateway (well-known 'RippleFox anchor'). No canonical /.well-known/xrp-ledger.toml at this domain — TOML absent, but on-chain Domain match + 11-year historical operation + real gateway site are sufficient evidence to lift the ticker_collision flag from XLM/ETH matches (which would otherwise render as 'issuer not on our verified list'). Two-way toml proof cannot be attempted (404 at /.well-known/); walker will not elevate to `verified`. Verdict per Charlie's 2026-09-12 audit: legitimate custodial/bridged issuer, neutral tier.
ripplefox.name: RippleFox — long-standing XRPL/Stellar custodial gateway
ripplefox.note: Custodial gateway issuing XRPL representations of XLM (native Stellar), CNY, and other assets. XLM on this issuer is a Ripplefox custodial IOU, not native Stellar — same class as GateHub-BTC or Bitstamp-USD: real gateway, real backing (custodial), no scam. Do NOT set ticker_collision=TRUE for these (issuer, ticker) pairs.
